verdicts.explanation: The 3.82 mS·cm⁻¹ room-temperature total conductivity for the 20% P-excess Na3.4 electrolyte is stated in the abstract and conclusions. The sintering conditions are only given per base composition (Na3.4 at 1300 °C), and the paper never states them for the P-compensated sample, so those two fields should be null.

The abstract states total conductivity rising from 1.60 to 2.95 mS·cm⁻¹ for Na3.4 powders calcined at 900 and 1200 °C, and the results sentence orders the two highest-calcination totals as Na3 (0.98) then Na3.4 (2.95). The Na3.4 sintering at 1300 °C for 12 h is stated in Methods, and no measurement temperature is given, so null is correct.

The results sentence gives total conductivities of 0.98 and 2.95 mS·cm⁻¹ for the highest-calcination electrolytes, in the order Na3 then Na3.4, so 0.98 belongs to Na3 calcined at 1100 °C. The Na3 sintering at 1225 °C for 12 h is stated in Methods, and no measurement temperature is given.
